title: Security Command Center Findings

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.3.30 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.3.30 search returns zero rows.

description: SCC aggregates misconfigurations and threats; operationalizing findings closes gaps faster than periodic console reviews.
value: Detecting security command center findings early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable continuous export or finding notifications to Pub/Sub. Map categories to owners. Auto-ticket CRITICAL; weekly review HIGH. Deduplicate by finding ID across updates.
visualization: Table (category, resource, severity), Bar chart (findings by category), Timeline (new findings).
knownFalsePositives: A fresh scanner run or a vendor re-rate can resurface a finding we already know about. We deduplicate on resource and time and we only escalate when the exposure is new or the severity stepped up.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` (Pub/Sub export) with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable continuous export or finding notifications to Pub/Sub. Map categories to owners. Auto-ticket CRITICAL; weekly review HIGH. Deduplicate by finding ID across updates.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" sourceProperties.ResourceName=*
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.30_security_command_center_30"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect security command center findings. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_30_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (category, resource, severity), Bar chart (findings by category), Timeline (new findings)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` (Pub/Sub export) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of security command center findings so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
